The regulations containing the general 
provisions governing the 1958 acreage 
reserve part of the Soil Bank Program, 
22 F. R. 6397, as amended and supple­
mented, are hereby further amended as 
follows:
1. Section 485.308 (b), as amended, is 
hereby further amended by adding the 
following at the end thereof; “In any 
case where a farm which during 1957 
participated in both the acreage reserve 
and conservation reserve programs is 
reconstituted for 1958, the acreage 
placed in the 1957 acreage reserve for 
any farm resulting from the reconstitu­
tion shall be determined as follows, both 
for the purposes of this paragraph and 
for the purposes of § 485.313 (f) (2 ):
(1) In the case of a division of a farm, 
the acreage for each commodity in the 
1957 acreage reserve shall be apportioned 
among the resulting farms on the same 
basis as the respective allotment was ap­
portioned; (2) in the case of a combina­
tion of two or more farms or parts of 
farms, the acreage placed in the 1957 
acreage reserve for the resulting farm 
shall be the sum of the acreage placed 
in the 1957 acreage reserve for each of 
the farms included in the combination 
for which a conservation reserve con­
tract was in effect for 1957, except that 
if only a part of a 1957 farm is combined 
with another farm the 1957 acreage re­
serve for such part shall be determined 
in accordance with subparagraph (1) of 
this paragraph.”

for disposition under the marketing

notify the office of the county committee

age and pay the cost of determining the 
adjusted acreage, except that in the case 
of wheat the producer shall not be re­
quired to pay such cost.”

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10314 at 16 FR 12709, in the Federal Register of December 19, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10314 and is signed December 17, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute, and provides that no member may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier. It directs that "The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; requires the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10314 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10314_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10314_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_522918d862.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed on January 9, 1952 pursuant to Executive Order 10314, and its title page is dated at New York, February 16, 1952; the report states that the parties stipulated to extend the time for the report to February 18, 1952 and that the President approved the extension. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the front matter of the board's report.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end; the held report records an approved extension to February 18, 1952, and its title page is dated February 16, 1952. That date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The thirty-day period after the report during which no change could be made except by agreement comes from section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the held sources do not show when the President received the report, so no exact end of that period is asserted, and its running out is a spent fact, not an end. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"The order's operative text has four elements: the creation of the board with the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report command, the Defense Production Act compliance sentence, and the sentence on unchanged conditions. None is independent of the board: the compliance sentence is a condition on how the board works, and the sentence on unchanged conditions opens by stating that it is made as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so its force comes from that statute. All share the order's end.","savings_check":"The enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 contains no saving or exception clause, and the ACT record for this pair lists none. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.","scope_check":"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause, and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right; a bounded search of the held Executive Order 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR disposition notes shows no residual effect.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188, Federal Register of January 8, 1952; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 10319, signed by Harry S. Truman and dated January 4, 1952; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier listed seventeen clauses, but sixteen of them are fee-schedule paragraphs (spirits of turpentine, rosin, drums, tank cars) of a Department of Agriculture naval-stores rule printed on the same Federal Register page after the order. I replace them with one whole-order clause running from the heading to the sentence ending "dispute arose." The order has three recitals and four operative sentences: the creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act with the rule that no member be interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; the direction that the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The order does not mention any other Executive order or any officer other than the President. Later facts: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 (PEB-100-Report.pdf) states that the board members were never named because the parties returned to direct negotiations, that the President granted three thirty-day extensions of time, that the parties reached an agreement dated April 24, 1952, and that no report to the President was made. The agreement date is recorded here as a spent fact and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24; The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held.  the board was never constituted (owner rulings of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines and on a board never constituted). Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order. The held-text number-citation scan in the packet lookups found no other held text citing 10319.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); here no report was ever made, according to the National Mediation Board record. (2) The three thirty-day extensions of reporting time named in that record extended the deadline only; their dates and instruments are not held, and an extension is not an end. (3) The status-quo period runs, by the order's own words, until thirty days after the board reports; no report was made, and the dispute was settled by agreement on April 24, 1952, so the order was functionally spent on that date but stayed on the books (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on a board never constituted: treat it like the other emergency-board orders until express revocation). (4) The section 502 compliance sentence is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the Defense Production Act is not held in this packet and no expiry of it is claimed as an end. (5) The OFR catalog and the number-citation scan show no instrument other than EO 12553 that revokes, supersedes or amends this order. No earlier end is shown.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the report direction and the section 502 compliance direction concern the board's work, and the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute and which ran only until thirty days after a report. The order creates no office, fund, delegation or right that outlived the board.","savings_check":"No savings or exception wording attaches to the EO 12553 revocation list. The settlement of the dispute is a completed private agreement, not a residual effect of the order.","scope_check":"EO 12553 revokes the order by number with no exception and reaches any amendments, so the single whole-order clause ends in full on that date. No amendment of the order is held."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 attaches no savings or exception clause to its revocation list (its enacting provision is one sentence followed by the table). The board was never constituted and made no report; the dispute was settled by the parties' own agreement of April 24, 1952, which is not a command of this order. No continuing right or duty arising from the order is shown.

The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10449 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board record (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10449_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10449_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_890e74e86f.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a National Mediation Board record for Emergency Board No. 104 stating that no members were appointed and that the parties reached agreement on April 26, 1953, so that no emergency board was set up for hearing the dispute; there is no report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on EO 10449 (a board never constituted is treated like the other emergency-board orders) the order stayed on the books until its express revocation; the fact that the board was never constituted is disclosed here, and the agreement of the parties on April 26, 1953 (a statement in that record) is a spent fact and not an end. The thirty-day report deadline (to May 24, 1953 on the inclusive reading) is a deadline and not an end. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10811 at 24 FR 3179 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 22, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 24, 1959 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 4297 to 4413 and 13450 to 14152 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, Air Transport Division, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars Pan American World Airways, Inc., or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10811 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10811_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10811_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_baa6c6b760.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 15, 1959 and a letter of transmittal dated Washington, D.C., June 12, 1959; the board states that the parties agreed to extend the time for the report to June 15, 1959. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 15, 1959 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 15, 1959 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 15, 1959 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 3567, the issue of April 26, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10875, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 22, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 22, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 130 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 8, 1960; the report's table of contents lists a letter of extension of the time limit. Thirty days after June 8, 1960 is July 8, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 8, 1960. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

Washington, Saturday , November  8, T  952
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10405
Exemption of T heodore M arks F rom 
Compulsory R etirement  for A ge
WHEREAS Theodore Marks, Associ­
ate Chief of the Veterans Employment 
Service, Department of Labor, during 
the month of November 1952 will become 
subject to compulsory retirement for 
age under the provisions of the Civil 
Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, 
as amended, unless exempted therefrom 
by Executive order; and WHEREAS, in my judgment, the pub­
lic interest requires that the said person 
be exempted from such compulsory re­
tirement as provided below:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 204 
of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 
(5 U. S. C. 715a),J hereby exempt the 
said Theodore Marks from compulsory 
retirement for age for an indefinite pe­
riod of time.
H arry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
November 6, 1952.
[F. R. Doc. 52-12058; Filed, Nov. 6, 1952;
4:14 p. m.]
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10406
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I n ­
vestigate a D ispute  B etween  the 
United A ir Lines , I nc., and C ertain of 
Its E mployees  >
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the United Air Lines, Inc., a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Flight Engineers’  International As­
sociation, UAL Chapter, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt 
interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the United Air Lines, Inc., or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.
H arry S. T ruman
T he W hite H ouse,
November 6, 1952.
[F. R. Doc. 52-12059; Filed, Nov. 6, 1952;
4:14 p. m.]
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10407
Withholding  of S tate or T erritorial
I ncome T axes by F ederal A gencies
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 1  of the act of July 17, 1952, 
66 Stat. 765, section 301 of title 3 of the 
United States Code (as added by sec­
tion 10 of the act of October 31, 1951, 
65 Stat. 712), and as President of the 
United States, I hereby prescribe the 
following regulations governing agree­
ments to be entered into between the 
Secretary of the Treasury and any State 
or Territory, pursuant to the provisions 
of the said act of July 17, 1952, with 
respect to the withholding of State or 
Territorial income taxes from the com­
pensation of employees of the United 
States:1. Such an agreement shall be entered 
into by the Secretary of the Treasury 
within 120 days of the receipt of a re­
quest therefor by the Secretary from the 
Governor or any other proper official

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the International Association of Ma­
chinists, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by ifie, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees,or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense i Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.
H arry S. T ruman

WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pan American World Airways, Inc.,  
a carrier, and certain of its employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
way and Steamship Clerks, Freight Han­
dlers, Express and Station Employes, a  
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW,. THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or by its employees, in the  
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

carriers represented by the Eastern,

Conference Committees, designated in

hereof, and certain of their employees

made a part hereof, on the subject of  
certain wage demands made by the em­
ployees; and
WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Albany Port District Railroad and other  
carriers represented by the Eastern,  
Western and Southeastern Carriers’  
Conference Committees, designated in  
list C attached hereto and made a part  
hereof, and certain of their employees  
represented by the cooperating (non­
operating) railway labor organizations  
designated in list D attached hereto and  
made a part hereof, on the subject of de­
mands of the employees for changes in  
agreements covering health and welfare  
benefits; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to*  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate the said disputes. No  
member of the said board shall be pecu­
niarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings ,  to 
the President with respect to the said
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order. *
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days'after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
changé, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Albany Port District Rail­
road and other carriers represented by  
the Eastern, Western and Southeastern  
Carriers’ •  Conference Committees or  
their employees in the conditions out of  
which the said dispute arose.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between

ment of the' National Mediation Board,

tial transportation service:

By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States it is  
ordered as follows:
Section 1. The third paragraph of  
Executive Order No. 9080 of February  
27,1942, authorizing the creation of the  
Joint Mexican-United States Defense  
Commission, is hereby amended to read  
as follows:
“ The United-States membership of the 
Commission shall consist of an Army  
m em ber, a Navy member, and an Air  
Force member, each of whom shall be  
designated by the Secretary of Defense  
and serve during the pleasure of the Sec­
retary. The Secretary shall designate  
from am ong the United States members  
the chairman thereof and may designate  
alternate United States members of the  
Commission.”
Sec. 2. The amendment made by 
section 1  hereof shall not be construed as 
terminating the tenure of any person  
who is a member, chairman, or alternate  
member of the United States section of  
the Commission on the date of this order,  
but such tenure may be terminated by  
the Secretary of Defense.

WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad and  
other carriers represented by the Eastern,  
western and Southeastern Carriers'  
Conference Committees, designated in
list attached hereto and made a part  
hereof, and certain of their employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, a labor organization;  
and
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Hoard,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate the said disputes. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
disputes within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Akron &  Barberton Belt  
Railroad Company and other carriers  
represented by the Eastern, Western and  
Southeastern Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittees or their employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said disputes arose.
D wight  D. E isenhower

DEFINITIONS
§  961.1 Act. “Act” means Public Act 
No. 10, 73d Congress, as amended and as 
re-enacted and amended by the Agricul­
tural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, 
as amended (7 U. S. C. 601 et seq.).
§  961.2 Secretary.  “Secretary” means 
the Secretary of Agriculture, or any of­
ficer or employee of the United States 
authorized to exercise the powers and to 
perform the duties of the Secretary of 
Agriculture.
§  961.3 Department of Agriculture.  
“Department of Agriculture” means the 
United States Department of Agriculture 
or any other Federal agency as may be 
authorized by Act of Congress, or by Ex­
ecutive order, to perform the price re­
porting functions of the United States 
Department of Agriculture.
§  961.4 Person. “Person” means any 
individual, partnership, corporation, as­
sociation, or any other business unit.
§  961.5 Philadelphia, Pennsylvania,  
milk, marketing area.  “Philadelphia, 
Pennsylvania, milk marketing area”, 
hereinafter called the “marketing area” 
means all the territory in the Common­
wealth of Pennsylvania situated within 
the following boundary line: Eeginning 
at a point in the Pennsylvania State line 
at the northern boundary of the Lower 
Makefleld township line in Bucks Coun­
ty, thence first westerly, thence southerly 
along said Lower Makefield township 
line to the Middletown township line; 
thence westerly and southerly along the 
Middletown township line to the Lower 
Southampton township line; thence 
northerly and thence westerly along the 
Lower Southampton township line to the 
Montgomery County line; thence north­
erly along the Montgomery County line
to the Trenton cut-off of the Pennsyl­
vania Railroad; thence westerly along 
said railroad to the Upper Dublin town­
ship line, thence along the southern and 
western boundaries of Upper Dublin 
township to the Whitemarsh township 
line; thence southerly along the White- 
marsh township line to the lower Merion 
township line; thence along the north­
ern boundary of lower Merion township 
to the Delawaré County line; thence 
northerly, westerly and southerly along 
the Delaware County line to the Pennsyl­
vania State line; thence ^easterly and 
northerly along the Pennsylvania State 
line to the point of beginning.
§  961.6 Cooperative association.  
“Cooperative association” means any 
cooperative marketing association of 
producers which the Secretary deter­
mines, after application by the associa­
tion:
(a) To be qualified under the provi­
sions of the Act of Congress of February 
18, 1922, as amended, known as the 
“Capper-Volstead Act”; and
(b) To have full authority in the sale 
of milk of its members and to be engaged 
in making collective sales of or market­
ing milk or its products for its members.
§  961.7 Producer milk plant.  “Pro­
ducer milk plant” means:
(a) A pasteurizing or bottling plant 
from which milk is disposed of during the 
month as Class I milk in the marketing 
area on routes (including routes oper­
ated by vendors), or through plant stores 
to retail or wholesale^utlets (except 
other producer milk plants) ; or
(b) Any other plant from which milk 
in the form of products designated as 
Class I milk (not including certified 
milk) is supplied during the month to a 
pasteurizing or bottling plant described 
in paragraph (a) of this section, any- 
part of which is allocated to Class I milk 
pursuant to §  961.47: Provided, That any 
such other plant shall not be included in 
this definition during any of the months 
of October, November, December and 
January in which shipments, any part of 
which is allocated to Class I milk, are 
made from the plant on less than 11 days 
during such month to such pasteurizing 
and bottling plant, or to a plant or plants 
supplying such pasteurizing or bottling 
plant unless such plant was a producer 
milk plant in at least four of £he pre­
ceding months of February through Sep­
tember: And provided further,  That in 
the case of a system operation in which 
the same handler operates both a pas­
teurizing and bottling plant(s) qualified 
as a producer milk plant(s) under para­
graph (a) of this section and two or more 
receiving plants qualified to ship milk to 
his pasteurizing and bottling plant(s), 
any of such qualified receiving plants as 
the handler may designate shall be con­
sidered as a unit (system) upon written 
notice to the market administrator set­
ting forth the plants to be included as 
a unit and the period during which such 
designation shall apply. Such notice 
and notice of any changes in designa­
tion, shall be furnished on or before the

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 10874
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE LONG ISLAND RAIL­
ROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF
ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
The Long Island Railroad Company, a 
carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U.S.C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by The Long Island Railroad Com­
pany, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

WHEREAS, under the authority 
vested in him by section 350 (a) of the 
Tariff Act of 1930, as amended by the 
act of June 12, 1934, entitled “An Act

Stat. 943), the time within which the

Chief of the Republic of Ecuador on

1951); and
WHEREAS Article X IX  of the said

ment shall remain in force and effect 
until six months from the day on which 
either Government shall give notice of 
its intention to terminate it; and 
WHEREAS, pursuant to the said Ar­
ticle X IX  the Government of the United 
States of America gave notice on July 
18, 1955, of its intention to terminate 
the said trade agreement; and 
WHEREAS the said section 350 (a) 
of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, 
authorizes the President to terminate, 
in whole or in part, any proclamation 
carrying out a trade agreement entered 
into under such section:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DWIGHT D. 
EISENHOWER, President of the United 
States of America, acting under and by 
virtue of the authority vested in me by 
the Constitution and the statutes, in­
cluding the said section 350 (a) of the 
Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, do 
proclaim that the said proclamation 
dated September 23, 1938, shall be 
terminated as of the close of January 17, 
1956, six months from the day on which 
notice of termination of the said trade 
agreement was given by the Government 
of the United States of America.
IN  WITNESS WHEREOF, I  have here­
unto set my hand and caused the Seal of 
the United States of America to be 
affixed.

twenty-seventh day of August in the year 
of our Lord nineteen hundred

pendence of the United States of 
America the one hundred and eightieth.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10314 at 16 FR 12709, in the Federal Register of December 19, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10314 and is signed December 17, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute, and provides that no member may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier. It directs that "The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; requires the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10314 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10314_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10314_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_522918d862.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed on January 9, 1952 pursuant to Executive Order 10314, and its title page is dated at New York, February 16, 1952; the report states that the parties stipulated to extend the time for the report to February 18, 1952 and that the President approved the extension. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the front matter of the board's report.
